logline: In 1940s Lahore, the women of the Heeramandi kotha navigate love, betrayal, and the independence movement as British colonial rule fractures the world they were born into.

renewal.note: Netflix renewed for Season 2 in June 2024, within five weeks of the premiere. Season 2 moves the courtesans from Lahore to the post-partition Indian film industry. No release date announced as of mid-2026.

bollymeter.basis: 46% on Rotten Tomatoes from 13 critics tracks a near-split reception: the visual spectacle is undeniable, but the consensus found pacing problems and thin characterisation behind the opulence.

pull_quotes.text: Heeramandi's lavish production design and sprawling cast are hampered by rote pacing and a grim treatment of its characters.
The series is visually stunning, but gets laboured and exhausting due to a weak storyline.
Bhansali's Netflix series mirrors his film-making's finest and frustrating features.

seasons.review_body: Heeramandi arrived on Netflix in May 2024 as Sanjay Leela Bhansali's first original series, with a reported production budget of 200 crore rupees. The eight-episode season follows the kothi women of Lahore's red-light district as the independence movement tugs at the world around them. The series centers period production design and costume work, with craftsmanship that reads as among the most ambitious on Indian streaming. The main objections come through in the narrative pacing, especially across the first five episodes, along with a screenplay that feels to prioritize spectacle over character psychology. The series also showed warmer engagement at 69 percent Popcornmeter, and it spent four weeks in Netflix's global non-English top ten, accumulating approximately 90.9 million hours viewed in its first month. The final three episodes landed with noticeably stronger reception than the middle run.

episode_reviews.title: Mallikajaan: The Queen of Heeramandi
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the kotha hierarchy with Manisha Koirala's Mallikajaan at its apex, and drops the season's two central conflicts: the mother-daughter power struggle within Heeramandi and the gathering storm of the independence movement outside its gates. The episode prioritises visual grammar over character grounding.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Mallikajaan descending the stairs for the first time - the series announcing its aesthetic register.

episode_reviews.title: Heeramandi: The Swan Song
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale brings the independence storyline to its culmination and resolves the season’s central power conflict. The last three episodes stand out as the strongest stretch of the season, and the finale lands better than the middle episodes.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The performance scene that folds political resistance into the classical mujra tradition - the visual argument the whole season was building toward.

critic_note.text: Feels slow until its last three episodes, where Bhansali's ambition finally coheres.
